rules.title: Escalation rules beat the mechanical permit
rules.statement: A mechanical substitution with an explicit stop condition may run at T0/E0 — but where an escalation rule also applies, the escalation wins.

rules.title: Distinct concepts are distinct types
rules.statement: Identifiers and domain scalars MUST NOT be interchangeable primitives. Each concept gets its own type.

rules.check: `adversarial-review.json` questions `architecture` and `contracts`, against the repository's domain vocabulary and strict-checker evidence

strategies.proposition: The adversarial reviewer compares the domain vocabulary and public contracts and rejects distinct identifiers or scalars that remain interchangeable primitives instead of distinct strict-checker-visible types.
strategies.residual: Review can miss two concepts with similar names, and distinct wrappers do not prove their conversions or invariants are correct.
strategies.must_pass: artifact:adversarial-review.json accepts the concept-to-type mapping under architecture and contracts
strategies.must_reject: artifact:adversarial-review.json rejects an unresolved primitive-interchangeability objection

migration.guidance: Use strict checkers after concepts are modeled; use structured review to decide which primitives represent distinct concepts.

rules.title: Ports are structural protocols
rules.statement: Retired because structural and nominal typing can both preserve inward dependencies when the boundary contract is owned by the ports role. The repository now declares its form and the conformance mechanism checks that source matches it.
rules.why: The v3 rationale incorrectly treated an adapter importing an inward port contract as dependency reversal. The relevant property is direction and typed conformance, not structural typing alone.
rules.failure_mode: The v3 rationale confused an allowed inward adapter-to-port import with dependency reversal and prescribed structural typing universally.

migration.guidance: Declare structural or nominal form per boundary and satisfy ARCH-024 instead of converting every boundary to Protocol.

rules.title: What the checker cannot enforce is enforced at runtime
rules.statement: Value ranges, cross-field invariants, ordering and temporal constraints, units, and stateful protocols MUST be enforced by boundary parsing or an explicit runtime contract, and stated in the docstring. They MUST NOT be assumed carried by an annotation.
rules.why: Any claim that strict typing guarantees correctness is false, and a contract that relies on it fails without ever having been checked.
rules.no_mechanism: Which constraints a checker *could* have carried is a judgement about the type system's reach on that expression, not a property of the syntax. `check:boundary_parsing` named this rule and never reported it.
rules.failure_mode: Any claim that strict typing guarantees correctness is false, and a contract that relies on it fails without ever having been checked.

rules.title: Signature or docstring, by who can enforce it

rules.title: Immutability is declared, and not mistaken for a guarantee
rules.statement: Frozen dataclasses, read-only mappings and final declarations MUST be used to signal intent; code MUST NOT rely on them being unbypassable.
rules.why: The freeze is shallow and can be circumvented; treating it as a hard guarantee produces an invariant nothing actually maintains.
rules.check: `adversarial-review.json` question `architecture`, against declared invariants, mutation ownership, and strict-checker evidence
rules.failure_mode: The freeze is shallow and can be circumvented; treating it as a hard guarantee produces an invariant nothing actually maintains.

strategies.proposition: The adversarial reviewer traces invariants through frozen values, read-only views, final bindings, and their owned mutation paths and rejects reasoning that treats shallow declarations as unbypassable runtime barriers.
strategies.residual: Review and static declarations can miss mutation through aliases, reflection, foreign code, nested mutable values, or deliberate bypasses.
strategies.must_pass: artifact:adversarial-review.json accepts the declared immutability assumptions and mutation ownership
strategies.must_reject: artifact:adversarial-review.json rejects an unresolved shallow-immutability objection
strategies.not_applicable: the repository owns no value or binding whose immutability participates in an invariant

migration.guidance: Retain frozen/read-only/final declarations where they communicate intent; review every invariant that depends on their shallow runtime behavior.

rules.title: Type sophistication stays proportionate
rules.statement: Type-level machinery SHOULD be introduced when it removes a class of defect, not to demonstrate that it can be.
rules.why: A signature only a specialist can read moves the comprehension cost onto every future reader, including the agent trying to repair it.
rules.no_mechanism: "Proportionate" is a judgment about the defect being prevented, which no check can weigh against the reading cost it imposes.
rules.failure_mode: A signature only a specialist can read moves the comprehension cost onto every future reader, including the agent trying to repair it.
